79801.sol: Eukaryotic ribosomes are produced in the nucleolus. Ribosomal proteins enter the nucleolus and combine with the four r RNA strands to create the two ribosomal subunits (one small and one large) that will make up the completed ribosome.

79939.sol: A food chain is a linear sequence of organisms through which nutrients and energy pass as one organism cats another. The food chain is represented as: Small plants zooplanktons Fish Man Primary Producer Primary consumer Sccondary consumer Tertiary consumer Related Theory

80006.subject: Botany
80006.text: In which of the following forms is iron absorbed by plants?
80006.sol: Plants obtain iron in the form of ferric ions ( Fe 3 + ). It is required in larger amounts in comparison to other micronutrients. It is an important constituent of proteins involved in the transfer of electrons like ferredoxin and cytochromes. It is reversibly oxidised from Fe 2 + to Fe 3 + during electron transfer. It activates catalase enzyme, and is essential for the formation of chlorophyll.

80170.sol: In C 4 plants, the fixation of carbon dioxide takes place in mesophyll cells with the help of enzyme PEPcase . The synthesis of sugar takes place in bundle-sheath cells with the help of RuBisCO enzymes.

80212.subject: Botany
80212.text: Photosynthetically active radiation (PAR) represents the following range of wavelength:
80212.sol: Photosynthetically Active Radiation (PAR) is the amount of light available for photosynthesis, which is light in the 400 to 700 ~nm wavelength range.

80413.subject: Botany
80413.text: Which of the following biomolecules is common to respiration mediated breakdown of fats, carbohydrates, and proteins?
80413.sol: The organic substances which are oxidised to produce energy during respiration are called respiratory substrates. Carbohydrates are the main respiratory substrates as our food contains 65-70% carbohydrates. The most preferred substrate is glucose as it is the most available carbohydrate. Fats are used as the respiratory substrate in deficiency of carbohydrates. Proteins are rarely used as a respiratory substrate. The flow of blood in arteries is fast as the blood in them is under great pressure. The pressure in pulmonary aorta is more than that in the pulmonary vein as it receives blood directly from right ventricle during ventricul

84226.subject: Zoology
84226.text: Which one of the following hormones though synthesized elsewhere, is stored and release by the master gland?
84226.sol: Neurohypophysis (pars nervosa) also known as posterior pituitary, stores and releases two hormones called oxytocin and vasopressin, which are actually synthesized by the hypothalamus and are transported axonally to the neurohypophysis. Oxytocin acts on the smooth muscles of our body and stimulates their contraction. In females, it stimulates a vigorous contraction of the uterus at the time of childbirth, and milk ejection from the mammary gland. Vasopressin acts mainly at the kidney and stimulates resorption of wat

84235.subject: Zoology
84235.text: Which of the following represents the action of insulin?
options: Increases blood glucose level by stimulating glucagon production.
Decreases blood glucose levels by forming glycogen.
Increases blood glucose levels by promoting cellular uptake of glucose.
Increases blood glucose levels by hydrolysis of glycogen.
84235.sol: Insulin is released by the ' cells' in the islets of Langerhans in response to food. Its role is to lower glucose levels in the bloodstream and promote the storage of glucose in fat, muscle, liver and other body tissues. ' cells' in the islets of Langerhans produce another important hormone, glucagon, which increase blood sugar levels. 84483.subject: Zoology
84483.text: Transplantation of tissues/organs fails often due to non-acceptance by the patient's body. Which type of immune-response is responsible for such rejections?
84483.sol: Non-acceptance or rejection of graft or transplanted tissues/organs is due to cell-mediated immune response. Cell-mediated immunity is defined as a beneficial host response characterized by an expanded population of specific T-cells, which, in the presence of antigens, produce cytokines locally.

84775.subject: Zoology
84775.text: Which of the following in sewage treatment removes suspended solids?
84775.sol: Primary treatment is a physical process which involves sequential filtration and sedimentation. Suspended solids are removed in stages; initially, floating debris is removed by sequential filtration. Then the grit (soil and small pebbles) are removed by sedimentation. All solids that settle form the primary sludge and the supernatant forms the effluent. The effluent from the primary settling tank is taken for secondary treatment.

84779.subject: Zoology
84779.text: Identify the microorganism which is responsible for the production of an immunosuppressive molecule cyclosporin A:
84779.sol: Trichoderma species are free-living fungi found in the root ecosystem (rhizosphere). The fungus Trichoderma polysporum is responsible for the production of cyclosporin A. It is used as an immunosuppressive drug and is used by organ transplant patients to avoid graft rejection.

101920.text: Assertion : In a pressure cooker the water is brought to boil. The cooker is then removed from the stove. Now on removing the lid of the pressure cooker, the water starts boiling again. Reason : The impurities in water bring down its boiling point.

If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
101920.sol: The pressure cooker works on the principle that boiling point of a liquid increases with increase of vapour pressure above the liquid. When the cooker is removed from the stove and the lid is removed, pressure again decreases due to which its boiling point decreases and water starts boiling again.

So, (+4) and (+2) are the common oxidate states (O.S.) for C to Pb . However, the stability of (+4) O.S. decreases from Ge to Pb ( Ge < Sn < Pb ) due to inert pair effect. Therefore, Ge forms stable compound in (+4) O.S. and Pb in (+2) O.S. (II) & (III) are correct. Stability of dihalides increases down the group. (IV) is incorrect.

107003.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Reason (R): The valence electron configuration of Mg is 3s² and that of Al is 3s² 3p¹ , whereas their univalent cations Mg ⁺ and Al ⁺ have 3
options: Both (A) and (R) are true but (R) is NOT the correct explanation of (A).
Both (A) and (R) are true and (R) is the correct explanation of (A).
107003.sol: Assertion (A) is true: The first ionization enthalpy of Mg is greater than that of Al . However, the second ionization enthalpy of Mg is lower than that of Al . Reason (R) is true and correctly explains (A): The first electron in Mg is removed from a fully filled and more penetrating 3s orbital ( 3s² ), requiring more energy than the removal of the 3p¹ electron in Al . For the second ionization, the electron is removed from Mg ⁺ ( 3s¹ ) and Al ⁺ ( 3s² ). Because Al ⁺ has acquired a stable fully filled 3s² configura

107093.subject: Chemistry
107093.text: What is the purpose of the Molecular Orbital (MO) Theory?
options: To understand the electronic configuration of elements
107093.sol: The Molecular Orbital (MO) Theory is one of the theories used to predict molecular shapes.

107360.subject: Chemistry
107360.text: What is the result of having hybrid orbitals directed in preferred directions?
options: Maximum electron repulsion between electron pairs
Formation of molecules with random shapes
Achieving a stable arrangement with minimum electron repulsion
107360.sol: Hybrid orbitals are directed in preferred directions to achieve a stable arrangement with minimum electron repulsion.

107921.subject: Chemistry
107921.text: The correct statement with regard to H ₂⁺ and H ₂⁻ is
options: both H ₂⁺ and H ₂⁻ are equally stable
both H ₂⁺ and H ₂⁻ do not exist
H ₂⁻ is more stable than H ₂⁺
H ₂⁺ is more stable than H ₂⁻
107921.sol: H ₂⁺: 1 s^1, 1 s^0 Bond order = 1 2 H ₂⁻: 1 s^2, 1 s^1 Bond order = 2-1 2 = 1 2 The bond order of H ₂⁺ and H ₂⁻ are same but H ₂⁺ is more stable than H ₂⁻ . It is due to the presence of one electron in the antibonding molecular orbital in H ₂⁻ .

108077.subject: Chemistry
108077.text: What effect does high altitude have on atmospheric pressure?
options: It has no effect on atmospheric pressure.
108077.sol: At high altitudes, atmospheric pressure is low.

108110.subject: Chemistry
108110.text: How does the volume of a gas depend on the number of molecules, according to Avogadro's law?
options: Volume is directly proportional to the number of molecules.
Volume is inversely proportional to the number of molecules.
Volume is not related to the number of molecules.
Volume depends on the temperature, not the number of molecules.
108110.sol: Avogadro's law states that the volume of a gas is directly proportional to the number of molecules of the gas.

108121.subject: Chemistry
108121.text: What happens to Z values at very low pressures for all gases?
options: Z is approximately 1, and the gases behave as ideal gases.
108121.sol: At very low pressures, Z is approximately 1 for all gases, and they behave as ideal gases.

108296.subject: Chemistry
108296.text: In the context of entropy, what distinguishes between a reversible and irreversible process?
108296.sol: The change in entropy (∆S) distinguishes between reversible and irreversible processes. For a reversible process, ∆S is zero, while for an irreversible process, ∆S is not zero.

108751.subject: Chemistry
108751.text: Assertion : The increase in internal energy ( E) for the vapourization of one mole of water at 1 ~atm and 373 ~K is zero. Reason : For all isothermal processes, E=0 .
options: If both assertion and reason are true and the reason is the correct explanation of the assertion
If both assertion and reason are true and the reason is not the correct explanation of the assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
108751.sol: At 373 ~K or 100^ C , the water starts boiling and at this temperature the vaporization of water is an isothermal process. The internal energy change ( E) , depend only on temperature, it follows that at constant temperature, the internal energy of the gas remains constant, i.e. E is zero.

108887.subject: Chemistry
108887.text: What does the subscript 'c' indicate in the equilibrium constant expression K c ?
108887.sol: The subscript 'c' in the equilibrium constant expression Kc indicates that it is expressed in concentrations of mol L-1 (concentration of reactants and products).

109324.subject: Chemistry
109324.text: Classify the following species into Lewis acids and Lewis bases and show how these act as such c) H +
options: Neither Lewis Acid nor Lewis Base

109340.subject: Chemistry
109340.text: Question: Why does the conductivity of an aqueous solution of sugar differ from that of a solution containing sodium chloride, and how is this difference affected by changes in sodium chloride concentration?
options: Sugar ionizes completely in water, while NaCl does not ionize, leading to different conductivities.
Sugar ionizes partially in water, while NaCl ionizes completely, resulting in varied conductivities.
Sugar does not ionize in water, but NaCl ionizes completely, causing differences in conductance.
Sugar ionizes fully in water, while NaCl ionizes partially, influencing their conductivities.
109340.sol: Correct Option is : (C) Sugar does not ionize in water, but NaCl ionizes completely, causing differences in conductance.

109930.subject: Chemistry
109930.text: What is the commercial meaning of a 30% solution of hydrogen peroxide?
109930.sol: A 30% solution of hydrogen peroxide contains 3% H 2 O 2.

109936.subject: Chemistry
109936.text: In what form does hydrogen primarily exist in the earth's crust and the oceans?
109936.sol: The paragraph suggests that hydrogen primarily exists in the earth's crust and the oceans in the form of hydrides.

109949.subject: Chemistry
109949.text: What type of compound does hydrogen form with elements?
109949.sol: The paragraph states that hydrogen combines with elements to form hydrides and a large number of covalent compounds.

110108.subject: Chemistry
110108.text: How is dihydrogen stored when it is converted into a liquid state?
options: It is stored in high-pressure cylinders
It is stored in tanks made of metal alloys
It is stored in open containers
It is stored in glass containers with stabilizers
110108.sol: Dihydrogen is stored in tanks made of metal alloys when it is converted into a liquid state.

110129.subject: Chemistry
110129.text: Would you expect the hydrides of N, O and F to have lower boiling points than the hydrides of their subsequent group members?
options: Yes, because N, O, and F hydrides have weaker intermolecular forces.
No, because N, O, and F hydrides have stronger covalent bonds.
Yes, because N, O, and F hydrides have larger molecular sizes.
No, because N, O, and F hydrides have stronger hydrogen bonding due to high electronegativity
110129.sol: Correct Option is : (D) No, because N, O, and F hydrides have stronger hydrogen bonding due to high electronegativity

111628.subject: Chemistry
111628.text: How are the names of straight chain saturated hydrocarbons typically structured?
options: They end with the suffix '-ene' and carry a numerical prefix.
They end with the suffix '-ane' and carry a prefix indicating the number of carbon atoms in the chain.
They end with the suffix '-ol' and carry a prefix indicating the number of hydrogen atoms in the chain.
They end with the suffix '-ine' and carry a prefix indicating the number of double bonds.
111628.sol: The names of straight chain saturated hydrocarbons end with the suffix '-ane' and carry a prefix indicating the number of carbon atoms in the chain.

112063.subject: Chemistry
112063.text: Which can not behave as a nucleophile for S _ N 2 reaction?
112063.sol: In S _ N 2 reaction, nucleophile transfers electron pair to carbon of substrate, leading to the formation of transition state. H ₂ O is a neutral nucleophile while CN ⁻, NH ₂⁻ and I ⁻ are negatively charged nucleophile. Thus, H ₂ O cannot behave as a nucleophile for S _ N 2 reaction.

112382.subject: Chemistry
112382.text: What is the product formed when vicinal dihalides undergo dehydrohalogenation?
112382.sol: Vicinal dihalides undergo dehydrohalogenation to form an alkene by eliminating one molecule of hydrogen halide.

options: A term used to describe highly ordered and crystalline structures.
A term used to describe solids with a disordered atomic arrangement lacking a regular repeating pattern.
A term used to describe metals.
A term used to describe liquids.

113865.subject: Chemistry
113865.text: Why is salt sprinkled on snow-covered roads in hilly areas to aid in clearing them, and what phenomenon is responsible for this process?
options: Salt increases friction between tires and snow, aiding traction.
Salt lowers the freezing point of water, causing snow to melt.
Salt absorbs sunlight, accelerating snow melting.
Salt chemically reacts with snow, breaking it down into water and minerals.
113865.sol: Correct Option is : (B) Salt lowers the freezing point of water, causing snow to melt.

114081.subject: Chemistry

114081.sol: The voltage of the cell on the voltmeter keeps on decreasing as time passes in the Daniell cell when the circuit is closed.

114482.sol: NaCl and CaCl ₂ are added to provide conductivity to the electrolyte and also to lower the fusion temperature of anhydrous MgCl ₂ .

options: Fe 2 O 3 , Al 2 O 3 , and SiO 2
115509.sol: Bauxite ore usually contains impurities like SiO 2 , iron oxides, and titanium oxide (TiO 2 ).

115547.subject: Chemistry
115547.chapter: General Principles and Processes of Isolation of Metals
115547.text: What substance is produced when zinc carbonate undergoes calcination?
115547.sol: Calcination of zinc carbonate produces zinc oxide (ZnO) and carbon dioxide gas (CO 2 ).

116520.subject: Chemistry
116520.text: Which two transition metals have trihalides beyond Mn in the 3d series?
116520.sol: Beyond Mn, no metal has a trihalide except FeX3 and CoF3.

117438.subject: Chemistry
117438.text: In tetrahedral complexes, are low spin configurations commonly observed?
options: It depends on the metal-ligand combination.
It depends on the metal's position in the periodic table.
117438.sol: In tetrahedral complexes, low spin configurations are rarely observed because the orbital splitting energies are not sufficiently large to force pairing.

117524.subject: Chemistry
117524.text: Coordination compounds are widely present in which of the following?
117524.sol: Coordination compounds are widely present in minerals, plants, and animal worlds.

117741.subject: Chemistry
117741.text: Given below are two statements: Assertion (A): Square planar complexes of type MABCD do not exhibit optical isomerism. Reason (R): Square planar complexes possess a plane of symmetry containing the central metal atom and all four ligands. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
117741.sol: Optical isomerism is exhibited by chiral molecules, which lack a plane of symmetry. In square planar complexes of the type MABCD , all four ligands and the central metal atom lie in the same plane. This molecular plane itself acts as a plane of symmetry. Since the molecule is superimposable on its mirror image, it is achiral and does not exhibit optical isomerism. Therefore, both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, and (R) is the correct explanation of (A). Answer: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the

118068.subject: Chemistry
118068.text: Two statements are given below Statement I: Chlorobenzene on nitration gives 1-chloro4-nitrobenzene as major product Statement II: Chlorobenzene undergoes nitration slowly than benzene Identify the correct answer
options: Statement I correct but statement II is incorrect
Statement II correct but statement I is incorrect
118068.sol: Thus, Statement I is correct. Since - Cl is a ring-deactivating group, so it slows down the electrophilic substitution reactions like nitration. Thus, Statement II is also correct.

118124.subject: Chemistry
118124.text: Give reason why haloalkanes react with KCN to form alkyl cyanides as main product while AgCN forms isocyanides as the chief product.
options: KCN is a strong nucleophile that attacks the carbon atom bearing the halogen, leading to the formation of alky
KCN is predominantly ionic and provides cyanide ions in solution. Although both carbon and nitrogen atoms are
The high reactivity of silver ions in AgCN promotes the formation of isocyanides as the major product.
The choice between alkyl cyanides and isocyanides as the product depends on the reaction temperature, with low
118124.sol: Correct Option is : (B) KCN is predominantly ionic and provides cyanide ions in solution. Although both carbon and nitrogen atoms are in a position to donate electron pairs, the attack takes place mainly through carbon atom and not through nitrogen atom since C—C bond is more stable than C—N bond. However, AgCN is mainly covalent in nature and nitrogen is free to donate electron pair forming isocyanide as the main product.

118372.subject: Chemistry
118372.text: Which functional group is formed when an alcohol reacts with an alkyl halide in a nucleophilic substitution reaction?
118372.sol: When an alcohol reacts with an alkyl halide in a nucleophilic substitution reaction, an ether functional group is formed.

118602.subject: Chemistry
118602.text: Given below are two statements, one is labelled as Assertion A and the other is labelled as Reason R Assertion A:- Butylated hydroxyl anisole when added to butter increases its shelf life. Reason R:- Butylated hydroxyl anisole is more reactive towards oxygen than food. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:-
options: Both A and R are correct and R is the correct explanation of A.
A is correct but R is not correct.
A is not correct but R is correct.
Both A and R are correct but R is NOT the correct explanation of A.
118602.sol: Antioxidants are important and necessary food additives. These help in food preservation by retarding the action of oxygen on food. They act through several chemical mechanisms. Butylated hydroxy anisole (BHA) is one of the familiar antioxidant. The addition of BHA to butter increases its shelf life from months to years as it is more reactive towards oxygen than food. Hence, both Assertion and Reason are correct and Reason is the correct explanation of Assertion.

120244.text: What was the first effective antibacterial agent prepared by Paul Ehrlich?
120244.sol: In 1932, Paul Ehrlich succeeded in preparing the first effective antibacterial agent, prontosil.

120571.subject: Chemistry
120571.text: What are carbohydrates that yield two to ten monosaccharide units on hydrolysis called?
120571.sol: Oligosaccharides are carbohydrates that yield two to ten monosaccharide units on hydrolysis.

121101.subject: Botany
121101.text: As we go from species to kingdom in a taxonomic hierarchy, the number of common characteristics
121101.sol: Lower taxa share more common characteristics as compared to higher taxa. So, as we go from species to kingdom in a taxonomic hierarchy, the number of common characteristics decreases. as we go higher from species to kingdom, the number of common characteristics goes on decreasing. Lower the taxa, more are the characteristics that the members within the taxon share. Higher the category, greater is the difficulty of determining the relationship to other taxa at the same level. Hence, the problem of classification bec

121255.subject: Botany
121255.text: The basic unit of classification is
121255.sol: The basic unit of classification is species. It is the lowest category of classification. It is a group of closely related individuals with similar morphological, anatomical, biochemical and cytological characters. It is a group of naturally interbreeding population with ability to produce fertile offsprings. Individuals of a species share a common gene pool. Species is reproductively isolated, thus genetically closed system. Species has the real existence in nature. The term 'species' was given by John Ray, an Eng

121339.subject: Botany
121339.text: What type of reproductive structure do phycomycetes produce?
121339.sol: Members of phycomycetes are found in aquatic habitats and on decaying wood in moist and damp places or as obligate parasites on plants. The mycelium is aseptate and coenocytic. Asexual reproduction takes place by zoospores (motile) or by aplanospores (non-motile). These spores are endogenously produced in sporangium. A zygospore is formed by fusion of two gametes. These gametes are similar in morphology (isogamous) or dissimilar (anisogamous or oogamous). Some common examples are Mucor, Rhizopus (the breadmould men

121740.subject: Botany
121740.text: How many flagella do the zoospores of brown algae have?
121740.sol: The members of phaeophyceae or brown algae are found primarily in marine habitats. They show great variation in size and form. They range from simple branched, filamentous forms (Ectocarpus) to profusely branched forms as represented by kelps, which may reach a height of 100 meters. They possess chlorophyll a, c, carotenoids and xanthophylls. They vary in color from olive green to various shades of brown depending upon the amount of the xanthophyll pigment, fucoxanthin present in them. Food is stored as complex car

122053.subject: Botany
122053.text: In which of the following pairs of plants do the male and female gametophytes NOT have an independent free-living existence?
122053.sol: In bryophytes (such as Sphagnum, Marchantia, and Polytrichum) and pteridophytes (such as Dryopteris and Pteris), the gametophytes have an independent, free-living existence. In gymnosperms (such as Pinus and Cycas) and angiosperms, the male and female gametophytes do not have an independent free-living existence. They remain within the sporangia retained on the sporophytes. Answer: Pinus and Cycas

122056.subject: Botany
122056.text: Match the plant parts of gymnosperms in List I with their characteristic features in List II. List I List II A. Pinus roots I. Coralloid roots B. Cycas roots II. Unbranched C. Pinus stem III. Mycorrhiza D. Cycas stem IV. Branched Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
122056.sol: In gymnosperms, different genera exhibit distinct morphological features. Roots: Pinus has a symbiotic fungal association in the form of mycorrhiza. Cycas has small specialised roots called coralloid roots that associate with nitrogen-fixing cyanobacteria. Stems: The stems are branched in Pinus and Cedrus, whereas they are unbranched in Cycas. Therefore, the correct match is A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II. Answer: A-III, B-I, C-IV, D-II

122643.subject: Botany
122643.text: Torsion of visceral mass is seen in animals belonging to class
122643.sol: Animals of class-Gastropoda of phylumMollusca undergo twisting or torsion of the visceral mass during development, leading to conversion of symmetrical embryo into an asymmetrical adult.

122737.subject: Botany
122737.text: How many floral appendages does a tetramerous flower have?
122737.sol: A flower may be trimerous, tetramerous or pentamerous when the floral appendages are in multiple of 3, 4 or 5, respectively. Flowers with bracts-reduced leaf found at the base of the pedicel - are called bracteate and those without bracts, ebracteate.

122842.subject: Botany
122842.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: A few millimetres above the root cap is the region of meristematic activity. Reason: The cells of this region are very small, thin-walled and with dense protoplasm .
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
122842.sol: A few millimetres above the root cap is the region of meristematic activity. The cells of this region are very small, thin-walled and with dense protoplasm. They divide repeatedly.

123092.subject: Botany
123092.text: Endosperm is consumed by developing embryo in the seed of
123092.sol: Endosperm, if present acts as the food storage tissue of a seed. The seeds with endosperm are called endospermic or albuminous (eg, cocos nucifera, Ricinus communis, Zea mays and other cereals, while those without endosperm are called non-endospermic or ex-albuminous seeds (eg, Brassica campestris, Arachis hypogea, Pisum sativum). In castor (Ricinus communis) the endosperm is whitish soft mass rich with oily reserve food material. The endosperm in maize is yellowish in colour, the outermost layer of endosperm is ca

123210.subject: Botany
123210.text: Which of the following tissues are not considered part of the ground tissue?
123210.sol: All tissues except epidermis and vascular bundles constitute the ground tissue . It consists of simple tissues such as parenchyma, collenchyma and sclerenchyma. Parenchymatous cells are usually present in cortex, pericycle, pith and medullary rays, in the primary stems and roots. In leaves, the ground tissue consists of thin-walled chloroplast containing cells and is called mesophyll.

123459.subject: Botany
123459.text: Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R). Assertion (A): Leaves of grasses curl inwards during severe water stress. Reason (R): During water stress, bulliform cells present on the adaxial epidermis become highly turgid, which makes the leaves curl inwards. In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given bel
options: Both (A) and (R) are correct and (R) is the correct explanation of (A)
Both (A) and (R) are correct but (R) is not the correct explanation of (A)
(A) is correct but (R) is not correct
(A) is not correct but (R) is correct
123459.sol: Assertion (A) is correct because in grasses, leaves curl inwards during severe water stress to minimise water loss by reducing the exposed surface area. Reason (R) is incorrect because the inward curling of leaves is caused when the bulliform cells become flaccid due to water stress. When these cells absorb water and become turgid, the leaf surface is exposed, not curled. Answer: (A) is correct but (R) is not correct

123541.subject: Botany
123541.text: How long does the cell cycle take for yeast cells?
123541.sol: A typical eukaryotic cell cycle is illustrated by human cells in culture. These cells divide once in approximately every 24 hours. However, this duration of cell cycle can vary from organism to organism and also from cell type to cell type. Yeast for example, can progress through the cell cycle in only about 90 minutes. The cell cycle is divided into two basic phases: Interphase,M Phase (Mitosis phase)

124353.subject: Botany
124353.text: In a eukaryotic cell, the site for active synthesis of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) is characterized by which of the following structural features?
options: It is bounded by a single unit membrane.
It is not bounded by any membrane.
It is bounded by a double membrane.
It is located freely in the cytoplasm.
124353.sol: The site for active synthesis of ribosomal RNA (rRNA) in a eukaryotic cell is the nucleolus. According to NCERT, the nucleolus is a non-membranous structure present in the nucleoplasm. Since it is not bounded by any membrane, its content is continuous with the rest of the nucleoplasm. Single or double membrane-bound structures include organelles like vacuoles, lysosomes, mitochondria, and the nucleus itself, but not the nucleolus. Answer: It is not bounded by any membrane.

124874.subject: Botany
124874.text: Assertion : Light is one of the important factor in transpiration. Reason : It induces stomatal opening and closing. Therefore, transpiration increases in light and decreases in dark.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
124874.sol: Light has got no direct effect on the rate of transpiration but indirectly it affects the rate in two ways firstly by controlling the stomatal opening and secondly by affecting the temperature. With the increase in the light intensity the rate of transpiration increases because the stomata get opened and the temperature increases. 125331.subject: Botany
125331.text: What is the purpose of chloroplast alignment in mesophyll cells?
options: To get the optimum quantity of incident light
125331.sol: The mesophyll cells in the leaves have a large number of chloroplasts. Usually the chloroplasts align themselves along the walls of the mesophyll cells, such that they get the optimum quantity of the incident light. Within the chloroplast there is membranous system consisting of grana, the stroma lamellae, and the matrix stroma (Figure 11.2). There is a clear division of labour within the chloroplast. The membrane system is responsible for trapping the light energy and also for the synthesis of ATP and NADPH. In st

125877.subject: Botany
125877.text: How are chasmogamous flowers similar to flowers of other species?
options: They do not open at all
They have exposed anthers and stigma
They rely on wind for pollination
125877.sol: Autogamy: In this type, pollination is achieved within the same flower. Transfer of pollen grains from the anther to the stigma of the same flower lie close to each other so that self-pollination can occur. Some plants such as Viola (common pansy), Oxalis, and Commelina produce two types of flowers – chasmogamous flowers which are similar to flowers of other species with exposed anthers and stigma, and cleistogamous flowers which do not open at all. In such flowers, the anthers and stigma lie close to each other. W

126458.subject: Botany
126458.text: What is the R group in proteinaceous amino acids?
126458.sol: Based on the nature of R group there are many amino acids. However, those which occur in proteins are only of twenty types. The R group in these proteinaceous amino acids could be a hydrogen (the amino acid is called glycine), a methyl group (alanine), hydroxy methyl (serine), etc.

126497.subject: Botany
126497.text: What is the significance of the transition state structure?
options: It is the final structure of the product
It represents the highest energy state
It is a stable structural state
It is the structural transformation between substrate and product
126497.sol: The structure of substrate gets transformed into the structure of product(s). The pathway of this transformation must go through the so-called transition state structure. There could be many more ‘altered structural states’ between the stable substrate and the product. Implicit in this statement is the fact that all other intermediate structural states are unstable. Stability is something related to energy status of the molecule or the structure.

126715.subject: Botany
126715.text: Read the following statements regarding the classification of enzymes: (A) Transferases catalyse a transfer of a group, including hydrogen, between a pair of substrates. (B) Hydrolases catalyse the hydrolysis of ester, ether, peptide, glycosidic, C-C, C-halide or P-N bonds. (C) Lyases catalyse the removal of groups from substrates by hydrolysis leaving double bonds. (D) Isomerases include all enzymes catalysing inter
126715.sol: Statement (A) is incorrect because transferases are enzymes that catalyse the transfer of a group 'other than hydrogen' between a pair of substrates. Statement (B) is correct as hydrolases catalyse the hydrolysis of ester, ether, peptide, glycosidic, C-C, C-halide or P-N bonds. Statement (C) is incorrect because lyases catalyse the removal of groups from substrates by mechanisms 'other than hydrolysis' leaving double bonds. Statement (D) is correct as isomerases include all enzymes catalysing inter-conversion of op

127279.subject: Botany
127279.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The species diversity decreases as we move away from the equator towards the poles. Reason: The diversity of plants and animals is uniform throughout the world and shows a rather even distribution.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
127279.sol: The diversity of plants and animals is not uniform throughout the world but shows a rather uneven distribution. For many group of animals or plants, there are interesting patterns in diversity, the most well- known being the latitudinal gradient in diversity. In general, species diversity decreases as we move away from the equator towards the poles.

127876.subject: Zoology
127876.text: How many basic types of tissues do all complex animals consist of?
127876.sol: In the preceding chapters you came across a large variety of organisms, both unicellular and multicellular, of the animal kingdom. In unicellular organisms, all functions like digestion, respiration and reproduction are performed by a single cell. In the complex body of multicellular animals the same basic functions are carried out by different groups of cells in a well organised manner. The body of a simple organism like Hydra is made of different types of cells and the number of cells in each type can be in thous

128240.subject: Zoology
128240.text: In Pheretima, septa are absent between which segments ?
128240.sol: In Pheretima posthuma (earthworm) septa are absent between 3 / 4 and 9 / 10 segments.

128291.subject: Zoology
128291.text: What does LH stimulate in females?
128291.sol: Over-secretion of GH stimulates abnormal growth of the body leading to gigantism and low secretion of GH results in stunted growth resulting in pituitary dwarfism. Excess secretion of growth hormone in adults especially in middle age can result in severe disfigurement (especially of the face) called Acromegaly, which may lead to serious complications, and premature death if unchecked. The disease is hard to diagnose in the early stages and often goes undetected for many years, until changes in external features bec

128485.subject: Zoology
128485.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: Progesterone supports pregnancy. Reason: Progesterone also acts on the mammary glands and stimulates the formation of alveoli and milk secretion.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
128485.sol: Progesterone supports pregnancy. Progesterone also acts on the mammary glands and stimulates the formation of alveoli and milk secretion.

128537.subject: Zoology
128537.text: Hormone Function A. Oxytocin 1. Role in the regulation of the basal metabolic rate B. ADH 2. Regulation of a 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of our body C. T3 3. Stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules D. Melatonin 4. Acts on the smooth muscles of our body and stimulates their contraction
128537.sol: T3 plays a role in the regulation of the basal metabolic rate. Melatonin plays a role in regulation of a 24-hour (diurnal) rhythm of our body. ADH stimulates resorption of water and electrolytes by the distal tubules. Oxytocin acts on the smooth muscles of our body and stimulates their contraction

128603.subject: Zoology
128603.text: A specific hormone is responsible for stimulating vigorous contraction of the uterus at the time of childbirth. Identify the anatomical site where this hormone is synthesised.
128603.sol: The hormone responsible for stimulating vigorous contraction of the uterus at the time of childbirth is oxytocin. Although oxytocin is stored and released into the blood by the posterior pituitary (pars nervosa), it is actually synthesised by the hypothalamus and transported axonally to the neurohypophysis. Therefore, the correct site of synthesis is the hypothalamus. Answer: Hypothalamus

129594.subject: Zoology
129594.text: Which of the following structures are situated in the cortical region of the kidney? I. Malpighian corpuscle II. PCT (Proximal Convoluted Tubule) III. DCT (Distal Convoluted Tubule) IV. Loop of Henle V. Collecting duct
129594.sol: The DCTs of many nephrons open into a straight tube called collecting duct, many of which converge and open into the renal pelvis through medullary pyramids in the calyces. The Malpighian corpuscle, PCT and DCT of the nephron are situated in the cortical region of the kidney whereas the loop of Henle dips into the medulla. In the majority of nephrons, the loop of Henle is too short and extends only very little into the medulla.

129797.subject: Zoology
129797.text: What is the inner pleural membrane in contact with?
129797.sol: The outer pleural membrane is in close contact with the thoracic lining. whereas the inner pleural membrane is in contact with the lung surface. The part starting with the external nostrils up to the terminal bronchioles constitute the conducting part whereas the alveoli and their ducts form the respiratory or exchange part of the respiratory system. The conducting part transports the atmospheric air to the alveoli, clears it from foreign particles, humidifies and also brings the air to body temperature. Exchange p

130090.subject: Zoology
130090.text: Read the following statements regarding the human respiratory system: A. The conducting part transports atmospheric air to the alveoli and brings it to body temperature. B. The conducting part extends from the external nostrils up to the terminal bronchioles. C. All structures of the conducting part are supported by incomplete cartilaginous rings. Choose the correct option.
options: Statements A and B are correct
Statements A, B and C are correct
Statements A and C are correct
Statements B and C are correct
130090.sol: According to NCERT, the part starting with the external nostrils up to the terminal bronchioles constitutes the conducting part. Thus, statement B is correct. The conducting part transports the atmospheric air to the alveoli, clears it from foreign particles, humidifies and also brings the air to body temperature. Thus, statement A is correct. The trachea, primary, secondary and tertiary bronchi, and initial bronchioles are supported by incomplete cartilaginous rings. The terminal bronchioles are part of the conduc

130392.subject: Zoology
130392.text: Body System Function A. Muscular system 1. Structural support B. Skeletal system 2. Amoeboid movement C. Neural system 3. Coordination of movements D. Cytoskeletal system 4. Locomotion and movement
130392.sol: Muscular system: Responsible for locomotion and movement. Skeletal system: Provides structural support. Neural system: Coordinates movements. Cytoskeletal system: Involved in amoeboid movement.

130475.subject: Zoology
130475.text: Read the following four statements regarding disorders of the muscular and skeletal system: (A) Myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder affecting the neuromuscular junction, leading to fatigue, weakening, and paralysis of skeletal muscle. (B) Muscular dystrophy is a progressive degeneration of smooth muscle, mostly due to a genetic disorder. (C) Tetany is characterised by rapid spasms in muscle due to high Ca⁺⁺ i
130475.sol: Statement (A) is correct as myasthenia gravis is an autoimmune disorder that affects the neuromuscular junction of skeletal muscles. Statement (B) is incorrect because muscular dystrophy involves the progressive degeneration of skeletal muscle, not smooth muscle. Statement (C) is incorrect because tetany is caused by low Ca⁺⁺ in body fluid, not high Ca⁺⁺ . Statement (D) is incorrect because gout is caused by the accumulation of uric acid crystals, not urea crystals. Therefore, exactly three statements are incorrect

130696.subject: Zoology
130696.text: Read the following statements and choose the follwoing option: 1. Lippes loop is a non medicated IUD 2. Multiload 375 is a copper releasing IUD 3. Progestart is a hormone releasing IUD 4. Spermicidal creams, jellies and foams are usually used alongwith these barriers to increase their contraceptive efficiency.
130696.sol: Intra Uterine Devices are presently available as the non-medicated IUDs (e.g., Lippes loop), copper releasing IUDs (CuT, Cu7, Multiload 375) and the hormone releasing IUDs (Progestasert, LNG-20).

131024.subject: Zoology
131024.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: The opening of the vagina is often covered partially by a membrane called clitoris. Reason: The hymen is a tiny finger-like structure which lies at the upper junction of the two labia minora above the urethral opening.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
131024.sol: The opening of the vagina is often covered partially by a membrane called hymen. The clitoris is a tiny finger-like structure which lies at the upper junction of the two labia minora above the urethral opening.

131054.subject: Zoology
131054.text: Read the following Assertion and Reason and choose the correct option. Assertion: In human beings, menstrual cycles ceases around 50 years of age, that is termed as menopause. Reason: Cyclic menstruation is an indicator of normal reproductive phase and extends between menarche and menopause.
options: Both Assertion and Reason are true and Reason is correct explanation of Assertion
Both Assertion and Reason are true but the Reason is not the correct explanation of Assertion
Assertion is true but the Reason is false
Both Assertion and Reason are false
131054.sol: In human beings, menstrual cycles ceases around 50 years of age, that is termed as menopause. Cyclic menstruation is an indicator of normal reproductive phase and extends between menarche and menopause.

131113.subject: Zoology
131113.text: Read the following statements and choose the correct option: 1. Placenta acts as an exocrine tissue. 2. In the later phase of pregnancy, a hormone called Relaxin is secreted by the ovary 3. hCG, hPL and relaxin are produced by women only during pregnancy. 4. Decreased production of these hormones is essential for supporting the fetal growth, metabolic changes in the mother and maintenance of pregnancy.
131113.sol: Placenta acts as an endocrine tissue and produces several hormones like human chorionic gonadotrophins, human placental lactogen, estrogens, progestogens, etc. In the later phase of pregnancy, a hormone called Relaxin is secreted by the ovary hCG, hPL and relaxin are produced by women only during pregnancy. Increased production of these hormones is essential for supporting the fetal growth, metabolic changes in the mother and maintenance of pregnancy.

131358.subject: Zoology
131358.text: Gastrula is the embryonic stage in which
131358.sol: Transformation of the blastocyst into gastrula with primary germ layers by rearrangement of the cells is called gastrulation. In all the triploblastic animals three germ layers-ectoderm, mesoderm and endoderm are formed by characteristic morphogenetic movements.

131378.subject: Zoology
131378.text: The embryo at 16 celled stage is known as
131378.sol: The embryo at the 16 -celled stage is called the morula. It is the mass of cells resulting from the cleavage of the ovum before the formation of a blastula. Blastomere is any cells produced during cleavage. Blastula is the early development stage of a metazoan, following the morula stage and consisting of a single, spherical layer of cells that encloses a hollow, central cavity.

131647.subject: Zoology
131647.text: Select the incorrect statement for the given figure.
options: E-The a gene encodes a transacetylase.
D-The y gene codes for permease, which increases permeability of the cell to β-galactosides.
C-The z gene codes for beta-galactosidase (β-gal), which is primarily responsible for the hydrolysis of the di
B-Lactose is the substrate for the enzyme beta-galactosidase and it regulates switching on and off of the oper
131647.sol: The i gene codes for the repressor of the lac operon. The z gene codes for beta-galactosidase (β-gal), which is primarily responsible for the hydrolysis of the disaccharide, lactose into its monomeric units, galactose and glucose. The y gene codes for permease, which increases permeability of the cell to β-galactosides. The a gene encodes a transacetylase. Hence, all the three gene products in lac operon are required for metabolism of lactose. Lactose is the substrate for the enzyme beta-galactosidase and it regula

131829.subject: Zoology
131829.text: Read the following statements regarding the lac operon in E. coli: A. Glucose or galactose cannot act as inducers for the lac operon. B. Regulation of the lac operon by the repressor is referred to as positive regulation. C. The y gene codes for permease, which increases the permeability of the cell to -galactosides. D. The repressor of the operon is synthesized from the i gene only in the presence of lactose. How ma
131829.sol: Statement A is correct: NCERT explicitly states that glucose or galactose cannot act as inducers for the lac operon; only lactose or allolactose can. Statement B is incorrect: Regulation of the lac operon by the repressor is referred to as negative regulation, because the repressor protein turns off the operon. Statement C is correct: The y gene codes for permease, an enzyme that increases the permeability of the cell to -galactosides (lactose). Statement D is incorrect: The repressor protein is synthesised constit

131981.subject: Zoology
131981.text: hnRNA undergoes two additional process. Out of them in one process an unusual nucleotide (methyl GPT) is added to the 5 ' end of molecule. What would you called this?
131981.sol: The process of addition of methyl GPT at the 5^ end of hnRNA is known as capping. Enzyme guanly transferase catalyses this process. Cap is essential for the formation of mRNA-Ribosome complex. Translation is not possible if cap is lacking, because cap is identified by 18 SrRNA of ribosome unity.

132336.subject: Zoology
132336.text: What does the given figure represent?
options: The amino acid composition of the relevant portion of α-chain of haemoglobin from an individual with sickle-ce
The amino acid composition of the relevant portion of β-chain of haemoglobin from an individual with sickle-ce
The amino acid composition of the relevant portion of α-chain of haemoglobin from a normal individual
The amino acid composition of the relevant portion of β-chain of haemoglobin from a normal individual
132336.sol: The defect is caused by the substitution of Glutamic acid (Glu) by Valine (Val) at the sixth position of the beta globin chain of the haemoglobin molecule. The substitution of amino acid in the globin protein results due to the single base substitution at the sixth codon of the beta globin gene from GAG to GUG.

132393.subject: Zoology
132393.text: Concept Description A. Linkage 1. The physical exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes during meiosis B. Recombination 2. Genes that are located close to each other on the same chromosome and tend to be inherited together C. Crossing over 3. The formation of new combinations of alleles due to the exchange of genetic material D. Genetic map 4. A diagram that shows the relative positions of genes on
132393.sol: Linkage: Genes located close to each other on the same chromosome tend to be inherited together. Recombination: The formation of new combinations of alleles due to the exchange of genetic material. Crossing over: The physical exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes during meiosis. Genetic map: A diagram that shows the relative positions of genes on a chromosome.

132862.subject: Zoology
132862.text: A group or population of individuals having the potential to interbreed and produce sustainable and fertile offspring is called ____.
132862.sol: A group or population of individuals having the potential to interbreed and produce sustainable and fertile offspring is called species

133062.subject: Zoology
133062.text: Assertion: Jave Apeman, Peking man and Heidelberg man are the fossils of Homo erectus. Reason: Homo erectus evolved from Homo habilis.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
133062.sol: The fossil of Java Apeman was discovered from pleistocene rocks in central Java. The fossil of Peking man was discovered from the lime stone caves of Choukoutien near Peking while that of Heidelberg man was discovered in mid pleistocene. All these three fossils come under the category of Homo erectus. Homo erectus appeared about 1.7 million years ago in middle pleistocene. H . erectus evolved from Homo habilis. He was about 1.5-1.8 metres tall. He had erect posture. His skull was flatter than that of modern man. He

133107.subject: Zoology
133107.text: Human ancestors who left cave paintings were
133107.sol: array c|l Human Ancestor & Characteristic Feature Neanderthal man & array l Believe in " Immortality of soul ". Make tools of bones, stones, quartz array Cro-magnon man & array l Cave painting, highest cranial capacity Make use of fire array Java ape man & array l Mse nonsyllabic and nonarticulate language array array

133455.subject: Zoology
133455.text: Natural immunity barriers Example A. Cellular barrier 1. Natural Killer B. Physiological barrier 2. Interferons C. Cytokine barrier 3. skin D. Physical barrier 4. Tears from eyes
133455.sol: Cellular barrier: Natural Killer (NK) cells are part of the immune response that provides a cellular barrier against infections. Physiological barrier: Tears from the eyes contain lysozyme, which acts as a physiological barrier to prevent infections. Cytokine barrier: Interferons are cytokines that provide a barrier by interfering with viral replication in infected cells. Physical barrier: The skin acts as a physical barrier, preventing pathogens from entering the body.

133457.subject: Zoology
133457.text: Disease Vector A. Malaria 1. Female Aedes mosquito B. Filariasis 2. Female Anopheles msquito C. Amoebiasis 3. Female Culex Mosquito D. Chikungunya 4. Housefly
133457.sol: Malaria: Transmitted by the bite of the female Anopheles mosquito, which carries the Plasmodium parasite. Filariasis: Spread by the female Culex mosquito, which carries the Wuchereria bancrofti parasite. Amoebiasis: Typically transmitted through food or water contaminated by houseflies, which carry the Entamoeba histolytica cysts. Chikungunya: Caused by a virus transmitted by the bite of the female Aedes mosquito.

133642.subject: Zoology
133642.text: Assertion : Dope test is used to estimate the level of blood alcohol by analysing the breath of persons drinking alcohol. Reason : A drunken person usually feels tense and less talkative.
options: If both assertion and reason are true and reason is the correct explanation of assertion
If both assertion and reason are true but reason is not the correct explanation of assertion
If assertion is true but reason is false
If both assertion and reason are false.
133642.sol: Dope test is an official test to discover whether a person or animal taking part in a competition has been given any drugs (such as anabolic steroids, erythropoietin etc.) to make their performance better or worse. It is a type of blood test. Alcohol is not used in this purpose. Alcohol has an effect on cerebellum and it results into imbalanced muscular activities, posture etc.

134046.subject: Zoology
134046.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
134046.text: Somaclonal variation can be obtained by
134046.sol: Somaclonal variation refers to all types of variation occur in plants regenerated from cultured cells or tissues. Genetic changes take place in plant tissue culture and these changes are passed to their progenies. This technology can be used for disease resistance, improvement of quality and yield in plants.

134065.subject: Zoology
134065.chapter: Strategies for Enhancement in Food Production
134065.text: The name of Norman Borlaug is associated with
134065.sol: Norman Borlaug is associated with green revolution. The green revolution means an increase in the production of crops particularly cereal crops. Such as wheat, rice and maize.

134435.subject: Zoology
134435.text: What is the significance of the cloning of antibiotic resistance gene in E. coli?
options: It allowed for the maintenance of introduced DNA in the host and transfer to its progeny
It facilitated the identification of DNA with desirable genes
It demonstrated the process of linking a piece of DNA with a plasmid
It demonstrated the ability to multiply copies of a specific gene
134435.sol: When this DNA is transferred into Escherichia coli, a bacterium closely related to Salmonella, it could replicate using the new host’s DNA polymerase enzyme and make multiple copies. The ability to multiply copies of antibiotic resistance gene in E. coli was called cloning of antibiotic resistance gene in E. coli . .

134532.subject: Zoology
134532.text: What is the outcome of spreading transformed cells on agar plates containing an antibiotic?
options: Both transformed and untransformed cells will grow
Neither transformed nor untransformed cells will grow
134532.sol: There are several methods of introducing the ligated DNA into recipient cells. Recipient cells after making them ‘competent’ to receive, take up DNA present in its surrounding. So, if a recombinant DNA bearing gene for resistance to an antibiotic (e.g., ampicillin) is transferred into E. colicells, the host cells become transformed into ampicillin-resistant cells . If we spread the transformed cells on agar plates containing ampicillin, only transformants will grow, untransformed recipient cells will die. Since, du

134540.subject: Zoology
134540.text: What is the role of separating techniques in recombinant technologies?
options: To express foreign genes in host cells
To make recipient cells competent to receive DNA
134540.sol: If any protein encoding gene is expressed in a heterologous host, it is called a recombinant protein. The cells harbouring cloned genes of interest may be grown on a small scale in the laboratory. The cultures may be used for extracting the desired protein and then purifying it by using different separation techniques .

134935.subject: Zoology
134935.text: Separation of DNA, fragments is done by a technique known as :
134935.sol: With the help of Gel electrophoresis technique, separation of DNA fragments, based on their size (mol. wt) can take place. DNA fragments can be separated on Agarose gel with the help of electrode and can be visualised with the help of ethidium bromide under UV-light.

6a104ff48b46719ce7976cc9.subject: Physics
6a104ff48b46719ce7976cc9.text: Identify the pair of physical quantities that possesses the same dimensional formula as that of energy density.
options: Coefficient of viscosity and linear momentum
Specific heat capacity and latent heat
6a104ff48b46719ce7976cc9.sol: Energy density is defined as energy per unit volume. Dimensional formula of energy density = [M L^2 T⁻²] [L^3] = [M L⁻¹ T⁻²] Pressure is defined as force per unit area. Dimensional formula of pressure = [M L T⁻²] [L^2] = [M L⁻¹ T⁻²] Bulk modulus is defined as the ratio of volumetric stress to volumetric strain. Dimensional formula of bulk modulus = [M L⁻¹ T⁻²] [M^0 L^0 T^0] = [M L⁻¹ T⁻²] Thus, pressure and bulk modulus have the same dimensional formula as that of energy density. Answer: Pressure and bulk modulus

6a1bb6be107bf677676d9f6d.subject: Chemistry
6a1bb6be107bf677676d9f6d.text: An alkene X upon reductive ozonolysis ( O₃ , followed by Zn/H₂O ) yields a mixture of two isomeric ketones, Y and Z. It is observed that both Y and Z respond positively to the iodoform test. Which of the following is the correct IUPAC name of the alkene X?
6a1bb6be107bf677676d9f6d.sol: Reductive ozonolysis of an alkene cleaves the carbon-carbon double bond to form carbonyl compounds. Since the products Y and Z are both ketones, the original alkene X must be a tetrasubstituted alkene. For both ketones to respond positively to the iodoform test, they must be methyl ketones, meaning each must contain a CH₃-CO- group. Furthermore, Y and Z are isomeric, which means they must possess the same molecular formula. Evaluating the ozonolysis products for each given option: For 2,3-dimethylhex-2-ene, the str

6a2109b2219e1ae5a1722996.subject: Biology
6a2109b2219e1ae5a1722996.text: During aerobic respiration, electrons from FADH₂ are transferred to oxygen via the electron transport system (ETS). Arrange the following components in the correct sequence of electron flow: I. Cytochrome c II. Ubiquinone III. Cytochrome a₃ IV. Cytochrome bc₁ complex
6a2109b2219e1ae5a1722996.sol: During aerobic respiration, electrons from FADH₂ are transferred to Complex II (succinate dehydrogenase). From Complex II, electrons are passed to the mobile electron carrier Ubiquinone (II). Ubiquinone transfers the electrons to Complex III, which is the Cytochrome bc₁ complex (IV). Complex III then passes the electrons to another mobile carrier, Cytochrome c (I). 6a7a1ff8b856332cbf5e99bb.sol: The atomic radius generally increases down a group due to the addition of new electron shells. However, in Group 13, Gallium ( Ga ) has the electronic configuration [ Ar ] 3 d ¹⁰ 4 s ² 4 p ¹ . The completely filled 3d electrons offer poor shielding (or screening) for the outer electrons from the increased nuclear charge.
